title: Q3 Run-rate & Procurement 1:1 - prep
content:
Goal for 1:1 with Priya (finance director):
- Align on Q3 run-rate assumptions and areas we should flag for exec review.
- Get sign-off plan for two pending procurement requests (NVIDIA GPUs and third-party monitoring tooling).
- Confirm cadence for monthly spend reviews and who owns follow-ups.

Context / quick summary:
- Current run-rate (last 30d actuals extrapolated): ~$3.2M annualized (ARR not relevant - this is ops run-rate).
  - Cloud infra (compute + storage + egress): ~$1.9M run-rate (~59%).
  - People-related costs (headcount + contractors): ~$0.9M (~28%).
  - Tools, SaaS, licenses: ~$0.25M (~8%).
  - Misc (travel, recruiting, other one-offs): ~$0.15M (~5%).
- Q3 headcount plan: hiring freeze lifted for infra/serving teams; +6 FTEs planned (4 infra, 2 SRE) starting July - incremental run-rate impact ~+$0.65M annualized.
- We have two procurement requests pending approval that materially affect FY26 spend:
  1) Dedicated GPU expansion (NVIDIA H100 reserved nodes) - procurement form submitted.
     - Capex vs Opex? We structured as committed cloud credits + reserved nodes via partner; expected incremental run-rate impact: +$0.9M annualized if fully leased.
     - Business case: required to meet Dedicated SLAs for two anchor customers (expected to onboard in Q3).
     - Risk: if customers delay, we carry cost. Ask: can procurement be staged (partial reservation) or be tied to milestone?
  2) New monitoring / APM tool (third-party observability) - annual contract request ~$120k/year.
     - Benefit: reduced MTTI, better multi-tenant tracing for hosted API.
     - Ask: can we negotiate pilot + annual price cap? Need approval for pilot spend (~$30k) now.

Open questions I want to cover in 1:1:
- Procurement staging: ask Priya for guidance on gating procurement approval based on customer milestones vs. engineering ramp.
- Budget reallocation: can we move $200-300k from misc/travel recruiting to infra temporarily to cover partial reservation? (short term internal transfer).
- Spend review cadence: propose monthly ops review with infra/product owners and finance - confirm attendees and decision rights.
- Contingency: what contingency buffer should we keep for Q3 ramp? suggest 7-10% of run-rate (~$220-320k).

Proposed agenda (20-30m):
1) Quick numbers (5m): current run-rate + Q3 headcount impact.
2) Procurement requests (10m): GPUs (staging options) and APM pilot (approval for $30k).
3) Budget reallocation / contingency (8m): short-term moves, approval authority.
4) Next steps / owners (2-5m).

Detailed notes / talking points:
- GPUs: remind Priya of anchor customers and contract milestones (customer A signed LOI, expected production in Aug; customer B in evaluation with PoC in Jul).
  - Option A: full reservation now (fastest to guarantee capacity) - +$900k run-rate.
  - Option B: partial reservation (50%) + on-demand fallback - reduces immediate run-rate to +$450k but increases risk of temporary capacity issues.
  - Option C: delay until customer A hits production (use burst credits / spot for interim) - minimal spend now but greater risk to SLA.
  - My recommendation: partial reservation (Option B) + require engineering to commit to rollout schedule and customer go/no-go dates.

- APM tool: emphasize metrics we expect to regain (MTTR reduction target 30%, reduce paging noise). Pilot has defined success metrics. If pilot hits metrics, convert to annual. Ask for approval to spend pilot $30k from tools budget now.

- Headcount delta: hiring 6 FTEs - we should confirm timing (start dates) to model Q3 vs Q4 impact. Ask Priya: is there a preferred conservative model (assume all starts on 09-01) or realistic ramp (50% start July)? I prefer the realistic ramp for planning but we should show both in executive summary.

Action items I want to walk out with (owner in parens):
- Decision on GPU procurement staging (Priya).
- Approval for APM pilot $30k spend (Priya).
- Permission to reallocate up to $250k from misc/travel to infra short-term (Alex -> implement once approved).
- Confirm monthly ops spend review cadence and attendees (Priya + Alex to assemble invite).
- Engineering to provide firm customer go/no-go dates and rollout timeline by 2026-03-10 (Jordan).

Risks to call out explicitly:
- Over-committing GPU capacity if customers delay = wasted committed dollars.
- If we under-provision, risk SLA breaches for Dedicated customers and potential revenue loss / credits.
- Headcount start date slippage could materially change run-rate; need guardrails in monthly reviews.

Prep materials to attach to meeting invite:
- One-pager: Q3 run-rate summary (exported from budget model) - attach (I will export final numbers 02/25).
- Procurement forms (GPU form, APM contract summary).
- Customer anchor LOIs / timelines (redacted to level appropriate).

Notes to self before meeting:
- Bring clear ask for each procurement (dollar amount + approval type).
- Be ready with tradeoffs (partial reservation numbers vs full reservation).
- Keep conversation focused on decision points - avoid deep technical debate in this meeting.

Follow-up after meeting (skeleton):
- Send decision summary + action list within 24h (Alex).
- Update budget model to reflect approved path and circulate to execs (Alex / finance ops).
- Kick off procurement steps (if approved) and assign procurement owner (Procurement Ops).

TODOs (short):
- Export run-rate one-pager (Alex) - due 2026-02-25.
- Confirm customer production dates with Eng (Jordan) - due 2026-03-10.
- Get legal to review APM pilot SOW (Alex / Legal) - ping legal contact Priya recommended.

Quick reference numbers (for verbal):
- Current run-rate: $3.2M annualized.
- GPU full reservation incremental run-rate: ~$900k.
- GPU partial (50%) incremental run-rate: ~$450k.
- APM pilot: $30k now, ~$120k/year if converted.
- Suggested contingency: 7-10% (~$220-320k).

End.
